the-lives-of-the-twelve-caesars-volume-0: Old, stern, and honest, the general Galba became emperor at seventy-three when Nero fell — and lasted seven months. Suetonius shows a man whose very virtues made him unfit for the job: his strictness alienated the soldiers, who murdered him in the Forum. The first casualty of Rome's Year of the Four Emperors, and a lesson in the limits of virtue.
a-lady-s-life-on-a-farm-in-manitoba: Mary Georgina Caroline Hall describes her years keeping house on a Manitoba farm — the isolation, the work, the prairie winters, and the small triumphs of pioneer womanhood. Written with honesty and spirit, her memoir is a valuable woman's view of settling the Canadian West.
a-trip-to-manitoba: Mary Agnes FitzGibbon, a young Englishwoman, describes her trip to Manitoba — the prairie land, the settlers, the new life rising on the frontier. Her fresh, lively letters capture the West in the making. A charming woman's view of pioneer Canada.

podcast-tuckercarlson-N_ndIxdM1BA:
Journalist Glenn Greenwald joins Tucker Carlson to discuss Epstein, CNN host Jake Tapper's humiliation, and calls to strike Gaza with nuclear force. Greenwald, who broke the Snowden story, has no sacred cows in media or government. His hour here is fearless by habit.

Greenwald gives his reading of what the Epstein case still hides and who it protects. He tears into Tapper and the press corps over their Biden coverage. The pair also address the extreme rhetoric around Gaza with alarm. Skeptical and sharp viewers get a reporter's full indictment of the powerful.
mythology-of-aryan-nations-chowkhamba:
The Reverend George Cox wrote The Mythology of the Aryan Nations in the Victorian age. The Chowkhamba house in India later reprinted his survey. Cox was a clergyman drawn to the science of myth.

He compares tales from India, Persia, Greece, and the North. Sun heroes and dawn maidens recur in his scheme. Like many of his day, he read most myths as weather stories. That theory is dated now, yet the gathered tales retain value. The book shows comparative myth at its boldest, and why later scholars had to rebuild the field.
